evidence.quote: High purity (> 99.9 wt%) elemental powders of Ti, Al, V, Cr, and Mo with particle size of ≤ 15 μm were milled in stainless steel tanks for 30 h at 400 rpm. The stainless steel ball to powder weight ratio of 30:1.
Subsequently, the milled powders were sintered via SPS (SPS-1050) at 1200 ◦C for 5 min under vacuum with a uniaxial pressure of 40 MPa.
The bulk alloys were encapsulated in evacuated quartz tubes, annealed at temperatures ranging from 800 to 1100 ◦C for 2 h, as well as at 1200 ◦C for both 2 and 6 h, followed by air cooling.

Ultra-fine grain TiAlV0.5CrMo refractory complex concentrated alloy (RCCA) was prepared by using mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS)
The system demonstrates exceptional microstructural and phase stability after the heat treatment at 1200 ◦C for 6 h, with only a slight decrease in hardness to a value of 9.86 GPa.
the strength-plasticity trade-off was achieved after heat-treated at 1200 ◦C for 2 h, with a compressive yield strength of 2667 MPa and a plastic strain of 10.7% at room temperature.
the strength-plasticity trade-off was achieved after heat-treated at 1200 ◦C for 2 h, with a compressive yield strength of 2667 MPa and a plastic strain of 10.7% at room temperature.
Furthermore, this alloy demonstrated a compressive yield strength of 153 MPa at a temperature of 1100 ◦C without fracturing at a strain of 50%.
The excellent mechanical properties were attributed to the synergistic effects of lattice distortions, reduced dislocation density, weakened texture and refined grain structure.
The flow stresses exhibited typical dynamic recrystallization (DRX) characteristics at elevated temperatures.
